title: Finite self-injective dimension of a regular local ring
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme]. In the derived category $D(A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the complex $A[0]$ is isomorphic to a bounded complex of injective $A$-modules [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Thus there exist integers $a\leq b$ and a complex $I^\bullet$ with injective terms, $I^j=0$ for $j\notin[a,b]$, and $A[0]\cong I^\bullet$ in $D(A)$.

source.place: Tag 0AWX, lemma-regular-gorenstein, first assertion; with Tag 0A7B, definition-dualizing, and more-algebra.tex Tag 0A5S, definition-injective-dimension.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-finite-gl-dim] to the given regular local ring $A$. It supplies a finite nonnegative bound $d=\dim A$ such that every $A$-module has a projective resolution of length at most $d$. We shall construct the required injective complex supported in $[0,d]$.

source.place: Tag 0AWX, lemma-regular-gorenstein, first two sentences of the proof; algebra.tex Tag 00O7, proposition-regular-finite-gl-dim, final assertion

proof.text: For each $A$-module $M$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-projective-dimension-ext-characterization] with $X=M$, $Y=A$ and $n=d$, using the resolution bound from step 1. It gives $\operatorname{Ext}^{i}_A(M,A)=0$ for every $i\ge d+1$, with Ext as in [def-pc-ext]. In particular this vanishing holds for $M=A/T$ for every ideal $T\subseteq A$. No finite-generation restriction on $M$ is used.

source.place: Tag 0AWX, lemma-regular-gorenstein, proof, Ext vanishing; algebra.tex Tag 065R, lemma-projective-dimension-ext, (1) implies (2)

proof.text: The category of $A$-modules is abelian with enough injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-modules-enough-injectives]. Apply clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-injective-resolution-degree-zero], choosing both abelian categories there to be the category of $A$-modules. It gives an exact augmented injective resolution $0\to A\xrightarrow{\varepsilon}I^0\xrightarrow{\partial^0}I^1\to\cdots$ with $I^j=0$ for $j<0$. Put $J=\ker(\partial^d:I^d\to I^{d+1})$.

source.place: Tag 0A5T, lemma-injective-amplitude, proof of (3) implies (1), choice of resolution and final kernel; derived.tex Tag 013K, lemma-injective-resolutions-exist, (1)

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-injective-resolution-final-kernel] with $R=A$, $N=A$, exactly the resolution and kernel $J$ from step 3, and the nonnegative integer $d$ from step 1. For every ideal $T\subseteq A$, step 2 applied to $M=A/T$ gives the required $\operatorname{Ext}^{d+1}_A(A/T,A)=0$. Hence this same $J$ is injective.

source.place: Tag 0A5T, lemma-injective-amplitude, proof of (3) implies (1), final-kernel injectivity and truncation.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-injective-final-kernel-truncation] with $R=A$, $N=A$, the resolution of step 3 and its kernel $J$, injective by step 4. Its augmentation $e:A[0]\to L^\bullet$ induces $A[0]\cong L^\bullet$ in $D(A)$; all terms of $L^\bullet$ are injective and vanish outside $[0,d]$. Taking $a=0$ and $b=d$ proves every clause since $0\leq d$. The cited statement includes $d=0$, where $e^0:A\xrightarrow{\sim}J$.

source.place: Tag 0A5T, lemma-injective-amplitude, proof of (3) implies (1), final-kernel injectivity and truncation.
